summary: This note describes the Western Region in south Ghana, which runs from the Ivory Coast border in the west to the Central Region in the east. It names the twin city of Sekondi - Takoradi, the coastal town of Axim, and the hilly inland area around Elubo. It also covers Cape Three Points, Ghana's southernmost location, where crude oil was discovered in commercial quantities in June 2007.
one_line: Overview of Ghana's Western Region, its long coastline, main towns, and Cape Three Points, site of a 2007 commercial crude oil discovery.
key_facts: The Western Region is located in south Ghana.
The Western Region spreads from the Ivory Coast border in the west to the Central region in the east.
The Western Region includes the capital and large twin city of Sekondi - Takoradi on the coast.
The Western Region includes coastal Axim.
The Western Region includes a hilly inland area including Elubo.
The Western Region includes Ghana's southernmost location, Cape Three Points.
Crude oil was discovered in commercial quantities at Cape Three Points in June 2007.
The Western Region has a long coastline stretching from Ghana's border with Ivory Coast to the Western region's boundary with the Central Region on the east.
